_comment: THE GRAPH PLANE -- .fux/runtime/graph.json, derived and gitignored.
It had no declared shape at all, and it is the largest derived structure
fux writes: on this repo, 3 050 edges and 458 community assignments. It is
also the only derived file with NO guard of the DOCS_FIELDS kind -- the doc
table at least carries a field tuple the runtime version checks.
WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE BEING DISPOSABLE: `explain`, `graph` and `path` read
it, and it is one of DETERMINISTIC_FILES -- two builds of the same index
must produce byte-identical graph.json. A shape that drifts does not just
break a verb; it breaks a byte-identity assertion that is checked, so the
failure surfaces somewhere other than the change that caused it.

_doc: The whole file. Written with `sort_keys=False` and no indent -- the key
ORDER is therefore load-bearing here in a way it is not for the committed
record, because determinism comes from the writer emitting the same
sequence rather than from a sort. `communities` is built from a sorted
node list for the same reason.
COMMUNITIES ARE UNSEEDED AND THAT IS THE STRONGER GUARANTEE. Label
propagation is random twice over and the reflex is `random.seed(0)`; a
fixed seed does not survive a Python version that reorders a set. The
randomness was REMOVED instead -- sorted visit order, ties broken on the
smallest label -- and a test asserts the ABSENCE of the import by parsing

edges.doc: each element is [src, kind, dst, grade]

communities.doc: node id -> community label, emitted in sorted node order

_doc: One element of `edges`, a 4-tuple rather than an object: there are
thousands of them and the key names would be 60% of the file.
`grade` is where a model-derived edge is distinguishable from a declared
one, and the distinction is the whole reason the field exists -- it is
why `inferred` was retired as an INGEST MODE name, because INFERRED is
